answer: Defend an agent economy with randomized peer-audit juries: each epoch, lottery-drawn committees of established identities inspect a sample of new claims. Ballots pass through a prism of secrecy — sealed until all are cast, so jurors cannot herd. A sybil operator never knows which fakes will meet the jetty of auditors guarding the nectar of emissions; deep audits probe behavioral history, so each fake needs a full fabricated past. Bribing every possible jury costs more than the fraud earns. Limits: honest newcomers queue, and audit quality depends on the jury pool staying independent.
